world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: Kisseberth, Charles W. 2003 (Makhuwa P30 chapter, named on Glottolog makh1260 page)

sources.citation: Ngunga, Armindo & Osvaldo G. Faquir. 2011 [repr. 2012]. Padronização da Ortografia de Línguas Moçambicanas: Relatório do III Seminário. (Colecção As nossas línguas III.) Maputo: Centro de Estudos Africanos, UEM. 358 pp. Ch. 2.4 'Emakhuwa', pp. 70-78.
sources.note: Emakhuwa chapter lists 'Exirima, falada nos distritos Metarica e Cuamba' among the variants covered (p. 70) and under 'Tom' (p. 77) says only 'Emakhuwa é uma língua tonal' (tone not yet written pending training). No word-stress/acento statement for Emakhuwa (unlike the Cinyungwe and Cisena chapters of the same report, which state penultimate stress).

sources.citation: do Sacramento, José Vicente. 1906. Apontamentos soltos da língua macúa. Imprensa Nacional (archive.org apontamentossolt00jos).
sources.note: Coastal (Moçambique island) Makhuwa. 'Accentuação' §§7-13 concerns diacritics for open/close vowel quality ('agudo', 'grave', 'circumflexo'), not the position of word stress.

sources.citation: Bernardo, Maurício. 2017. Análise fonológica da estrutura verbal do passado recente em Emakhuwa. Dissertação de Mestrado, Universidade Eduardo Mondlane, Maputo.
sources.note: Central (Nampula) variant. Locates Exirima in Maúa, Metarica, Cuamba (Niassa). Lit. review: 'Bernardo (2009a) refere também que em algumas variantes de Emakhuwa, como Exirima, por exemplo, se verifica ainda o contraste de significados de palavras através do tom' (second-hand: Exirima has lexical tone contrasts). Cites Filippi & Frizzi 2005 and Massimaculo 2004. Nothing on stress/acento.

sources.citation: Kisseberth, Charles W. & Rozenn Guérois. 2014. Melodic H tones in Emakhuwa and Ecuwabo verbs. Africana Linguistica 20: 181-205.
sources.note: Tonal melodies across Ikorovere, Imitthupi, Imeetto, Esaaka, Eeratti, Enlai, Ilê, Mugeba; Eshirima not among them. 'In all dialects the tonal contrast is presence of H on a mora versus its absence.' No stress statement.

sources.citation: SIL Moçambique (Oliver Kröger, John David Iseminger). 2009 [electronic ed. 2010]. Notas gramaticais sobre Emakhuwa-Imeetto. Monografias Linguísticas Moçambicanas 6. Nampula: SIL.
sources.note: Meetto variety; alphabet + morphology only; no tone or accent section.

sources.citation: van der Wal, Jenneke. 2009. Word order and information structure in Makhuwa-Enahara. Utrecht: LOT (LOT 215; PhD Leiden). Ch. 2 'A short description of Makhuwa-Enahara', 2.2 Prosody pp. 28-35.
sources.note: Enahara variety (coastal Nampula), not Shirima. Tone: mora is TBU, nouns have 1-2 underlying Hs, verbs no lexical tone, High Tone Doubling + Final Lowering. p. 34: 'Makhuwa is clearly a tonal language.. Unlike these languages [Makonde, Makwe, Zulu, Sotho], Makhuwa does not have this penultimate lengthening.' p. 20: 'Makhuwa does not have automatic penultimate lenghtening as in other Bantu languages'. No statement on word stress.

sources.citation: Downing, Laura J. 2004. What African languages tell us about accent typology. ZAS Papers in Linguistics 37: 101-136.
sources.note: Survey; Bantu stress table (15) does not list Makhuwa. No information on Shirima.

sources.citation: Cassimjee, Farida & Charles W. Kisseberth. 1999. A conspiracy argument for Optimality Theory: Emakhuwa dialectology. University of Pennsylvania Working Papers in Linguistics 6(1): 81-96.
sources.note: Tone only (Ikorovere, Eerati, Esaaka): H vs toneless moras, no lexical tone in verb stems, doubling. Authors say they studied 'over twenty dialects' but Eshirima is not named. No stress statement.

sources.citation: Cheng, Chin-Chuan & Charles W. Kisseberth. 1979. Ikorovere Makua tonology (part 1). Studies in the Linguistic Sciences 9(1): 31-63 (read in archive.org scanned of SLS vol. 9).
sources.note: Ikorovere (Tunduru, Tanzania). Tone of verbs entirely predictable from stem length and morphology; phrase-final lowering. No word-stress statement.

sources.citation: Kisseberth, Charles W. 2003. Makhuwa (P30). In D. Nurse & G. Philippson (eds.), The Bantu Languages (Routledge Language Family Series), 546-565. London: Routledge.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Authoritative pan-dialectal sketch by the main Makhuwa tonologist; its phonology section is the best place for an explicit statement on tone vs. stress (and absence of penult lengthening) valid across dialects including Eshirima; named by Glottolog as the subclassification source for makh1260.

sources.citation: Frizzi, Giuseppe. 2008. Murima ni ewani exirima: biosofia e biosfera Xirima: antologia e gramática Xirima. Maúa: Centro de Investigação Xirima. 1785 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Contains a 'gramática Xirima' by the same Consolata missionary team; second chance at a Shirima-specific accent/tone statement.

sources.citation: Filippi, Mário Farmar & Giuseppe Frizzi. 2005. Dicionário Xirima-Português e Português-Xirima: gramática e alfabetização. Maúa, Niassa: Centro de Investigação Xirima. 1422 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: The only modern Shirima-specific work with a grammar section ('gramática e alfabetização'); likely states tone/accent conventions for Exirima.

sources.citation: Massimaculo, Pedro Alberto. 2004. Reduplicação verbal em Eshirima. Tese de licenciatura, Universidade Eduardo Mondlane, Maputo. 61 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Only Shirima-specific item in Glottolog; a UEM thesis on verbal reduplication would normally open with a phonological sketch (syllable, tone/acento) of Eshirima.

sources.citation: Cassimjee, Farida & Charles W. Kisseberth. 1999. Tone variation across Emakhuwa dialects. In S. Kaji (ed.), Proceedings of the Symposium Cross-Linguistic Studies of Tonal Phenomena: Tonogenesis, Typology, and Related Topics, 261-287. Tokyo: ILCAA, Tokyo University of Foreign Studies.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Survey of the tone systems of 20+ Emakhuwa dialects; the likeliest published source with Eshirima prosodic data and an explicit characterisation of the prosodic type.

sources.citation: Prata, António Pires. 1960. Gramática da língua macua e seus dialectos. Cucujães (Portugal): Escola Tipográfica das Missões, Sociedade Missionária Portuguesa. 454 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Glottolog's language note says it explicitly covers 'Chirima = Makhuwa-Shirima [vmk]' alongside other dialects; a Portuguese missionary grammar of this size almost certainly has an 'acento tónico' paragraph, which would be the only first-hand Shirima-covering stress statement. Glottolog (hh) holds a private scan.
